candidate.title: GUIDE-seq
candidate.scope: The GUIDE-seq row of the assigned Illumina poster: in-cell dsOligo integration at genomic DSBs, isolation/random shearing, end repair/UMI-adapter ligation and tag-specific PCR to indexed DNA. The title and expanded row label identify one assay (Genome-wide, unbiased identification of DSBs enabled by sequencing); spelling/capitalization GUIDE-Seq and the abbreviation dsODN refer to this same target and its tag. The verified collection page 36 has the same target and labels. Neighboring BLESS, DSB-Seq and EC-seq rows are independent catalogue entries, not depicted GUIDE-seq alternatives. The Tsai et al. primary implementation resolves the otherwise generic tag and adapter identities; this extraction does not assert that all later GUIDE-seq applications use identical chemistry. STAT-PCR remains an embedded operation. The graph ends at the depicted DNA library; the paper-supported sequencing/mapping interpretation is recorded on that product and amplification operation.

states.label: Genome DNA with double-strand breaks in living cells
features: Biological target: genomic DNA double-strand break sites; the diagram starts with a broken duplex, rather than an explicit nuclease cleavage operation.
The matched primary implementation tags blunt-ended RNA-guided-nuclease-induced breaks in living human cells.

states.label: dsOligo insert (dsODN tag)
features: A double-stranded DNA oligo drawn as a short red duplex entering the genomic break.

Paper-supported identity of the tag: a blunt 34-bp duplex with 5-prime phosphorylation and phosphorothioate protection near both the 5-prime and 3-prime ends of both strands; these end features are not encoded explicitly in the poster icon.
This shared oligo sequence supplies the tag-specific priming site; it is distinct from the random molecular index introduced during library preparation.

states.label: Tag-enriched, indexed DNA sequencing library
features: The final DNA icon is annotated Oligo tag; the preceding PCR/primer illustration labels P5, P7, Index 2 and Index 1.

Sequenced carrier: amplified DNA physically linking a tag-derived priming boundary with the adjacent genomic flank and adapter-derived library sequence; this is a library of captured integration junctions.
The random molecular index supports consolidation of PCR-derived duplicate reads. P5/P7 and sample indexes are library interfaces, distinct from the integration tag and UMI.

Paper-supported interpretation: mapping the adjacent genomic sequence localizes captured DSB sites; tag-directed amplification from the two tag strands can recover either genomic flank. The poster compresses this into one PCR block and draws no separate flank workflows.

Molecularly consolidated read counts report recovery of tag-bearing template fragments and can serve as a relative cleavage proxy in the evaluated system. They do not certify complete detection, perfect nuclease specificity, or the exact indel/translocation outcome at every captured site; RGN-independent breaks can also be tagged.

operations.label: dsOligo tag integrated in live cells
operations.description: The introduced dsOligo becomes integrated at genomic double-strand breaks in living cells, converting broken genomic loci into tagged integration junctions.
operations.mechanism: The matched primary implementation reports blunt dsODN capture by an end-joining process consistent with NHEJ. The schematic does not separately depict production of the breaks or nuclease delivery.
operations.information_effect: A known DNA tag becomes physically linked to genomic sequence at a captured break. This marks successful capture events, not all possible DSBs and not exclusively nuclease-induced off-target breaks.

operations.label: DNA isolation / Random shearing
operations.description: Tagged cellular genomic DNA is isolated and randomly fragmented, producing a DNA-fragment population containing integration-junction templates as well as untagged background. The diagram combines isolation and shearing into one block.
operations.information_effect: The relevant physical association retained in a tag-bearing fragment is the tag joined to its neighboring genomic sequence; the fragment ends provide sites for library-adapter attachment.

operations.label: End repair / Adaptor ligation
operations.description: The sheared DNA ends are prepared and sequencing adapters are attached. The output fragment examples bear adapter segments and the labeled UMIs, while retaining any integrated oligo tag.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper identifies the adapters as half-functional/single-tail adapters with a random molecular index. The broad poster block does not enumerate the internal end-processing reactions.
operations.information_effect: Introduces the adapter priming interface and a molecular identity on each original fragment for correction of PCR duplication. This step alone does not select tag-bearing genomic fragments.

operations.label: PCR / dsOligo-specific amplification
operations.description: Tag-specific amplification enriches adapter-ligated fragments carrying an integrated dsOligo and generates the final indexed DNA library. The PCR arrow, primer/amplicon illustration carrying P5/P7 and Index 1/Index 2, and the final Oligo tag DNA icon are treated as one broad amplification block.
operations.mechanism: The matched primary implementation uses tag-complementary and adapter-complementary primers in two rounds of nested anchored PCR, termed Single-Tail Adapter/Tag (STAT)-PCR. STAT-PCR is an embedded amplification component of GUIDE-seq. Priming from each dsODN strand recovers the adjacent genomic flanks; the diagram does not resolve the individual reactions or their pooling.
operations.information_effect: Enriches physical tag–genomic-flank linkage rather than all genomic fragments. The genomic flank supplies the mappable locus, the molecular index supports duplicate consolidation, and the depicted library ends/indexes supply sequencing/sample interfaces. Sequencing and mapping are the paper-supported readout interpretation; no sequencing or computational operation is added to the poster graph.
